evidence.quote: I am very comfortable at this point with a decision to start to taper our asset purchases before the end of the year and, preferably, as early as at our next meeting in November.
If the expansion continues as I expect, I will support a pace of tapering that would end our asset purchases by the middle of next year.
Nevertheless, I still see a material risk that supply-related pricing pressures could last longer than expected.
If elevated inflation readings continue into and through the next year, we may begin to see an imprint on longer-run inflation expectations.
maintaining a highly accommodative monetary policy stance at this stage of the economic expansion may pose risks to the stability of longer-term inflation expectations.
I don't expect that we will see employment fully return to pre-pandemic levels any time soon.

parsed.rationale: Bowman advocates starting taper as early as November and ending purchases by mid-2022, citing upside inflation risks, valuation pressures, and risks to inflation expectations. Her cautious employment outlook is attributed to supply factors not addressable by policy, so the net signal leans hawkish.
